questions.question: Marang Apparel: direct materials R495 000, direct labour R360 000, factory overheads R345 000, work-in-progress R45 000 at both the start and end of the year, fifteen thousand units finished. Build the production cost statement levels aloud and give the unit cost, then state where the R180 000 selling commission and R75 000 office salaries belong.
questions.expected_answer: Prime cost: 495 000 plus 360 000 is R855 000. Add factory overheads of R345 000 for a total cost of production of R1 200 000. Add opening work-in-progress of R45 000 and subtract closing work-in-progress of R45 000 — the adjustment cancels — giving cost of production of finished goods of R1 200 000. Unit cost: 1 200 000 over fifteen thousand is R80. The commission is a selling and distribution cost and the office salaries are administration; both live in the income statement and never enter the production cost statement, because a misfiled cost corrupts prime cost, total cost and unit cost at once.

questions.question: Using selling price R160, variable costs R110 per unit and fixed costs R420 000, calculate the break-even point, prove the R330 000 profit at fifteen thousand units two ways, and explain what happens to break-even if the selling price rises while costs stay unchanged.
questions.expected_answer: Contribution: 160 minus 110 is R50. Break-even: 420 000 over 50 is eight thousand four hundred units. Proof one: six thousand six hundred units beyond break-even times R50 is R330 000. Proof two: sales of fifteen thousand at R160 are R2 400 000, less variable costs of R1 650 000 and fixed costs of R420 000, leaves R330 000 — the two roads agree. A higher selling price widens the contribution per unit, so the same R420 000 of fixed costs is covered by fewer units and the break-even point falls; the safety margin between production and break-even widens, which is the interpretive sentence the marks want.

questions.question: A supplier's statement shows R51 800 against our ledger balance of R45 900. Our payment of R4 200 on the 31st is missing from the statement, the statement carries a R5 300 invoice for goods arriving only next month, and our ledger posted one invoice twice at R3 600. Reconcile both sides and state the general rule, then compute VAT owed from output R57 000, input R39 600, drawings of R6 000 excluding VAT and a bad debt of R2 300 inclusive.
questions.expected_answer: Statement side: 51 800 minus the 4 200 payment in transit minus the 5 300 invoice for undelivered goods gives R42 300. Ledger side: 45 900 minus the 3 600 duplicate gives R42 300 — agreement. Rule: timing differences sit on the statement side until the post catches up, and each side corrects only its own errors. VAT: 57 000 minus 39 600 is R17 400; drawings return the input claim, adding fifteen percent of 6 000, R900; the bad debt reclaims output of fifteen over one hundred and fifteen of 2 300, R300, subtracted. Amount owed to SARS: R18 000, money held in trust and never the business's own.
